chapter: Uniforms, funeral music and horn styles
title: Uniforms of the Tuxedo, Eureka and other bands; borrowed and secondhand outfits
summary: Rene describes the Tuxedo's blue uniform, the Eureka's black pants and white shirts, fireman caps, and buying cheap tuxedos for the Jefferson Tea Room.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: a lot of old things way back, boy. That's a parade outfit here. They never changed a customer costume, bro. They still got the same identity. Still got them white top caps, double-soar handkerchief around them and everything. They ain't done no better than uniform, I tell you. They're the same identical thing they use. Father ain't got a piece of stuff and I tell his wife take on my handkerchief and put some tape around and stick it over the cap. The same way they try to buy a uniform cap. No, indeed, man. The Eureka band was the honest one. The real hat and tuxedo, they had a uniform. They spent money for the band.
What kind of uniform would the tuxedo have on the street?

Oh, they had a, let's see, I see the uniform. They had a blue, a blue, a blue suit, blue sewage, you know, with a little short collar and a sardine glove, black trivet. I see the pictures there where they had a uniform. And the Eureka, they had the black pants and the white shirts.
Well, here's an old man Allen stand. Would the tuxedo thing look like that? Old man Allen stand. Would they have those kind of collars and everything?

Oh, yeah, yeah, that's right. That was a bad uniform. Yeah, that's the kind of uniform it had. That's the correct. You ain't got none of them there with the fireman caps there. Let's see if they, look at this.
What kind of cap was that?
Well, the ECC was to get the old suits for the fireman.

The brass band. Oh, catch me too. Sometimes they want us to play somewhere to show them. Many times we went and go around the fireman's house. I wore them many times. Had a police cap on and a fireman coat on. Mm-hmm. Yes, sir.
Well, this wouldn't be the kind of cap that goes up like this, you know, like they use when they're fighting fire or something. No, no. Just a regular cap of the bill.
No, no, just a regular cap of the bill, you see. Mm-hmm. That's a cap they would wear when they, you know, they're going through and forth to their jobs. Yeah, not a fighting cap.
What would happen when somebody would fill in for another guy as far as uniforms went?

Oh, well, most of all the fellas would find some kind of way to get them a uniform. Or if they didn't find them to get a uniform, they would just make them take off their coats and hats and everybody would be in white shirts. Especially if somewhere where they say, boy, and sometimes we had to have tuxedo suits. See, like we were playing the Jefferson Tee Room on a Friday night. In the Jefferson Tee Room, you know, in the Ardabon Park, we had to have a tuxedo suit on a Friday night, see. And we went and bought secondhand. Well, you used to go get them cheap on that one, you know, three and a half, four dollars, you'd get a tuxedo suit. That time, you had them in theaters, you know, and them actors wear all that costume stuff like that, they didn't leave all that stuff in the pressure shop. You could pick up everything, though.
